reason: No verified refutation stands: the round-1 team-game and winner-chooses refutations were fixed (free-for-all only, chooser always a loser), and Judge 3's round-2 turn-order ambiguity was removed when the tie-break moved to the winner picking among the tied first losers; round 3 filed nothing. The derivation holds step by step. 103.1 names 'the loser' as a single player (step 1), and with two or more losers in a multiplayer game it gives no way to pick one (steps 3-4, the gap). The stipulation in step 5 fills that gap and never conflicts with a quoted rule. In free-for-all (806.1) players compete as individuals, so 104.2c's early-loser-wins exception cannot arise and the winner is never one of the losers. A tied first loser is a player who lost, so the chooser always satisfies 103.1's 'loser' requirement. A game where all remaining players lose together is a draw under 104.4a and goes to 103.1's draw sentence, which step 6 leaves untouched, so the winner-based tie-break never meets a drawn game. I accept the stipulation as the rule: the earliest loser chooses, ties go to the winner's pick among them, and the draw sentence stays. Remaining points (a first loser who left the match, or a tie not stated as its own fact) are drafting gaps shared with 103.1, not contradictions of any rule I checked.

evidence.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.
If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.
In Free-for-All multiplayer games, a group of players compete as individuals against each other.
